title: SSC English 1st Paper Exclusive Model Test 2026-2027 | ১০০ নম্বরের ২টি চূড়ান্ত মডেল প্রশ্ন ও নির্ভুল সমাধান
content:
এসএসসি ও দাখিল পরীক্ষা ২০২৬ এবং ২০২৭ সালের পরীক্ষার্থীদের চূড়ান্ত প্রস্তুতিকে নির্ভুল ও সময়োপযোগী করতে ইংরেজি ১ম পত্রের পূর্ণাঙ্গ ১০০ নম্বরের মডেল টেস্ট অনুশীলন অত্যন্ত গুরুত্বপূর্ণ। জাতীয় শিক্ষাক্রম ও পাঠ্যপুস্তক বোর্ড (NCTB)-এর সর্বশেষ সিলেবাস ও প্রশ্ন কাঠামোর ওপর ভিত্তি করে তৈরি করা ২টি বিশেষ এক্সক্লুসিভ মডেল টেস্ট প্রশ্নপত্র এবং প্রতিটির পূর্ণাঙ্গ সমাধান নিয়ে এই বিশেষ স্টাডি গাইডটি তৈরি করা হয়েছে।

সারসংক্ষেপ (Quick Overview): এসএসসি ইংরেজি ১ম পত্র পরীক্ষায় পূর্ণমান ১০০ এবং নির্ধারিত সময় ৩ ঘণ্টা। প্রশ্নপত্রটি প্রধানত দুটি অংশে বিভক্ত: Part A: Reading Test (৭০ নম্বর) এবং Part B: Writing Test (৩০ নম্বর)। রিডিং অংশে পাঠ্যবইয়ের সিন প্যাসেজ (Seen Comprehension), কবিতা (Poems) এবং সাহিত্য ও ছোটগল্প (Literature & Stories) থেকে প্রশ্ন থাকে। আর রাইটিং অংশে স্টোরি রাইটিং, ডায়লগ, ইনফরমাল লেটার বা ইমেইল থাকে। এই আর্টিকেলে বোর্ড প্রশ্ন মানের ২টি পূর্ণাঙ্গ মডেল টেস্ট এবং প্রতিটি প্রশ্নের আদর্শ উত্তরপত্র (Model Answers) অন্তর্ভুক্ত করা হয়েছে।
পরীক্ষার্থীদের জন্য জরুরি পরীক্ষা হল নির্দেশিকা: ইংরেজি পরীক্ষার ৩ ঘণ্টা সময় কীভাবে সঠিকভাবে বণ্টন করবেন, ওএমআর শিট পূরণের নিয়ম এবং পরীক্ষার হলের সতর্কতা সম্পর্কে বিস্তারিত জানতে পড়ুন আমাদের অফিশিয়াল গাইড: পরীক্ষার হলের ৫টি জরুরি নিয়মাবলি ও নির্দেশিকা দেখুন →

সূচিপত্র: বিষয়বস্তুর পূর্ণাঙ্গ রূপরেখা

পরীক্ষার বিভাগ (Part) প্রশ্নের ধরন ও বিষয়বস্তু প্রশ্ন সংখ্যা নির্ধারিত নম্বর

২. এক্সক্লুসিভ মডেল টেস্ট ০১: প্রশ্নপত্র (Full Marks 100)

SSC / DAKHIL EXAMINATION 2026-2027

English First Paper [Regular] | Subject Code: 107/136

Time: 3 Hours | Full Marks: 100

Part A — Reading Test (Marks: 70)

Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions no. 1, 2 and 3:

"Zahir Raihan was one of the most talented film makers in Bangladesh. He was born on 19 August 1935 in the village Majupur, now in Feni district. He was an active worker of the Language Movement. He was one of the ten students to go out in a procession on 21 February 1952 despite a ban on such activities. As a result, he and many others were arrested and taken to prison. Zahir was also present at the historic meeting of Amtala on 21 February 1952. He also took part in the mass movement in 1969. In 1971, he joined the Liberation War. All through his life, Zahir dreamed for a democratic society, a society that will ensure freedom of speech and will. He had many dreams about our film industry too. He made a legendary film 'Jibon Theke Neya' based on the Language Movement of 1952. In this film, an autocratic woman symbolizes the military dictator Ayub Khan in East Pakistan. On 30 December 1971, someone informed Zahir about an address somewhere at Mirpur, where he might find his brother, the famous writer Shahidullah Kaiser, who had gone missing from 14 December 1971. Zahir left home to get his brother back, but he never returned."

1. Choose the correct answer from the following alternatives: (1 x 7 = 7)

  1. Zahir Raihan was born in — (i) Dhaka (ii) Feni (iii) Chittagong (iv) Comilla
  2. What was Zahir Raihan's dream throughout his life? — (i) to be rich (ii) to establish a democratic society (iii) to be a politician (iv) to live abroad
  3. The film 'Jibon Theke Neya' is based on — (i) 1971 war (ii) 1969 mass movement (iii) 1952 Language Movement (iv) Six-point movement
  4. The word 'legendary' means — (i) infamous (ii) renowned/celebrated (iii) ordinary (iv) unknown
  5. Zahir Raihan went to Mirpur to find his — (i) father (ii) son (iii) missing brother (iv) friend

2. Answer the following questions: (2 x 5 = 10)

  1. What do you know about Zahir Raihan's childhood and background?
  2. Why was Zahir Raihan arrested in 1952?
  3. When did he take part in the mass movement?
  4. What is the symbolic significance of the film 'Jibon Theke Neya'?
  5. Why is Zahir Raihan considered a freedom fighter though he was primarily a film maker?

3. Fill in each gap with a suitable word based on the text: (1 x 5 = 5)

Zahir Raihan was an active (a) ______ of the Language Movement. He had a great (b) ______ to establishing a democratic society. He reflected the political crisis of Pakistan through his (c) ______ 'Jibon Theke Neya'. He also joined the (d) ______ War in 1971. Unfortunately, he disappeared while searching for his missing (e) ______.

4. Answer the following questions from poems (Any 5 out of 8): (3 x 5 = 15)

  1. Do you like the poem "Two Mothers Remembered"? Why?
  2. What should children do to show gratitude to their mothers?
  3. Why did the traveler stop by the woods in Robert Frost's poem?
  4. How has the poet described the sea in "The Sands of Dee"?
  5. What things are offered by the poet to the old gipsy man in "Time, You Old Gipsy Man"?
  6. What do you understand by the line "Each Book is a Magic Box"?
  7. Who is the poet of the poem "Time, You Old Gipsy Man"?

5. Answer the following questions from stories (Any 5 out of 8): (3 x 5 = 15)

  1. Who was Portia? What do you know about her wisdom?
  2. How did Portia save Antonio's life in the court of Venice?
  3. Who was Shylock and why did he hate Antonio?
  4. Sketch the character of Antonio as a loyal friend.
  5. Who walked towards Antonio with a knife and what was the condition of the bond?

Part B — Writing Test (Marks: 30)

10. Completing a Story: (15 Marks)

"Robert Bruce was a famous king. Once his kingdom was invaded by enemies. He fought courageously but lost the battle. In order to save his life, he fled away and took shelter in a remote cave. He was in a pensive mood when suddenly he noticed a spider..."
Task: Complete the story in your own words. Give an attractive title and state the moral.

11. Dialogue Writing: (15 Marks)

Suppose you are Bakul and your friend is Nayon. Write a dialogue between you and your friend about your preparation for the upcoming SSC examination.

৩. এক্সক্লুসিভ মডেল টেস্ট ০১: পূর্ণাঙ্গ সমাধান (Model Answers)

মডেল টেস্ট ০১ এর নির্ভুল সমাধান ও উত্তরপত্র (Solution Sheet)

Answer to Question No. 1 (MCQ):

  • (a) (ii) Feni
  • (b) (ii) to establish a democratic society
  • (c) (iii) 1952 Language Movement
  • (d) (ii) renowned / celebrated
  • (e) (iii) missing brother

Answer to Question No. 2 (Short Questions):

  • (a) Childhood & Background: Zahir Raihan was born on 19 August 1935 in the village Majupur in Feni district. He was an exceptionally talented intellectual, writer, and pioneer filmmaker of Bangladesh.
  • (b) Reason for arrest in 1952: He was arrested because he was one of the brave ten students who violated Section 144 and brought out a historic procession on 21 February 1952 demanding Bengali as a state language.
  • (c) Mass movement participation: He actively participated in the mass movement of 1969 against the oppressive military regime of Ayub Khan.
  • (d) Significance of 'Jibon Theke Neya': The film is an allegory where an autocratic housewife represents dictator Ayub Khan, inspiring the nation to fight for democracy.
  • (e) Freedom fighter status: Though a filmmaker, Zahir joined the 1971 Liberation War directly and projected the Pakistani genocide to the global audience through his documentary 'Stop Genocide'.

Answer to Question No. 3 (Gap Filling):

(a) worker / activist | (b) commitment / dedication | (c) film / masterpiece | (d) Liberation | (e) brother

Answer to Question No. 4 (Poem Solutions):

  • (c) Robert Frost's Woods: The speaker stopped by the dark woods to admire the tranquil beauty of falling snow and seek temporary solitude from life's hectic routine.
  • (e) Gifts offered to Time: The poet offered bells for Time's jennet, a great golden ring, peacocks bowing, boys singing, and sweet girls decorating Time with May flowers.
  • (f) 'Each Book is a Magic Box': A book is called a magic box because, like magic, opening a book unlocks realms of imagination, knowledge, and wonder for the reader.

Answer to Question No. 5 (Merchant of Venice Solutions):

  • (b) How Portia saved Antonio: Disguised as a young lawyer Balthazar, Portia cleverly pointed out that Shylock's bond allowed only a pound of flesh but not a single drop of Christian blood. If any blood was shed, Shylock's goods would be confiscated. This loophole completely disarmed Shylock.

Answer to Question No. 10 (Model Completing Story):

Perseverance Brings Success: King Robert Bruce and the Spider

Robert Bruce, the king of Scotland, fought six times against King Edward I of England to free his motherland, but was defeated every time. Despairing and hopeless, he hid in a secluded cave. While lying there, he saw a tiny spider trying to reach the cave roof with its thread. Six times the spider fell down, but on the seventh attempt, it successfully reached the roof. The spider's relentless determination inspired King Bruce. He realized that failure is the pillar of success. Bruce gathered his soldiers once more, fought with renewed vigor, and successfully liberated Scotland.
Moral: Failures are the stepping stones to success. Try and try until you succeed.

৪. এক্সক্লুসিভ মডেল টেস্ট ০২: প্রশ্নপত্র (Full Marks 100)

SSC / DAKHIL EXAMINATION 2026-2027

English First Paper [Model Test 02] | Subject Code: 107/136

Time: 3 Hours | Full Marks: 100

Part A — Reading Test (Marks: 70)

Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions no. 1, 2 and 3:

"Humans can neither change the sun's radiation nor the earth's orbit around the sun. But they can control the increase in the amount of greenhouse gases and its effect on the atmosphere. Only during the last hundred years, the concentration of carbon dioxide in the air has increased by 30 percent, and this has happened mostly because of burning fossil fuels. Coal, mineral oil, and natural gas are burned for generating energy, driving vehicles, and running industrial factories. As a result, huge amounts of carbon dioxide are released into the air daily. Furthermore, massive deforestation has reduced the earth's capacity to absorb carbon dioxide. If we do not reduce the consumption of fossil fuels and stop cutting trees, the global temperature will continue to rise, leading to catastrophic climate changes, melting polar ice caps, and rising sea levels that could submerge low-lying coastal countries like Bangladesh."

1. Choose the correct answer from the following alternatives: (1 x 7 = 7)

  1. What can humans NOT change? — (i) forest areas (ii) earth's orbit around the sun (iii) pollution levels (iv) factory production
  2. Carbon dioxide has increased by — in the last hundred years. — (i) 10% (ii) 20% (iii) 30% (iv) 50%
  3. Which fossil fuel is burned for energy? — (i) water (ii) coal and gas (iii) solar power (iv) wind
  4. The word 'catastrophic' means — (i) beneficial (ii) disastrous / destructive (iii) peaceful (iv) slight
  5. What could happen to low-lying countries? — (i) flourish (ii) submerge under water (iii) turn into deserts (iv) expand

2. Answer the following questions: (2 x 5 = 10)

  1. What are the primary causes of the increase in carbon dioxide?
  2. How does deforestation contribute to the greenhouse effect?
  3. Why is Bangladesh particularly vulnerable to global warming?
  4. What measures should humans take immediately to save the planet?
  5. Define the role of renewable energy in reducing greenhouse gases.

3. Fill in each gap with a suitable word: (1 x 5 = 5)

Fossil fuels are burned at an alarming rate due to rapid (a) ______. Coal is one of the fuels used for (b) ______ electricity. Our atmosphere is being polluted for the (c) ______ of greenhouse gases day by day. Our (d) ______ on fossil fuels must be reduced. We should not destroy our (e) ______ which play a vital role in producing oxygen.

4. Literature & Stories Section (Any 5 out of 8): (3 x 5 = 15)

  1. Who brought the news of Mr. Brently Mallard's death in 'The Story of an Hour'?
  2. How did Mr. Mallard supposedly die according to the rumour?
  3. Who was Rosamond and what did she want to buy in 'The Purple Jar'?
  4. Why was Antonio brought to the court of justice?
  5. Who was Portia and how did she show her legal genius?

5. Poetry Section (Any 5 out of 8): (3 x 5 = 15)

  1. What is the central theme of the poem "Time, You Old Gipsy Man"?
  2. Why does the poet ask Time to pause its relentless journey?
  3. Who was Mary in the poem "The Sands of Dee"? How did she drown?
  4. What does Robert Frost mean by "miles to go before I sleep"?

Part B — Writing Test (Marks: 30)

10. Formal Letter / Email Writing: (15 Marks)

Write an email to the Headmaster of your school requesting permission and financial assistance to arrange an English Language Club for SSC students.

11. Dialogue Writing: (15 Marks)

Write a dialogue between two friends regarding the importance of tree plantation to combat catastrophic climate change.

৫. এক্সক্লুসিভ মডেল টেস্ট ০২: পূর্ণাঙ্গ সমাধান (Model Answers)

মডেল টেস্ট ০২ এর নির্ভুল সমাধান ও উত্তরপত্র (Solution Sheet)

Answer to Question No. 1 (MCQ):

  • (a) (ii) earth's orbit around the sun
  • (b) (iii) 30%
  • (c) (ii) coal and gas
  • (d) (ii) disastrous / destructive
  • (e) (ii) submerge under water

Answer to Question No. 2 (Short Questions):

  • (a) Causes of CO2 increase: The rapid burning of fossil fuels (coal, oil, and natural gas) for power, vehicles, and industries is the primary cause.
  • (b) Role of deforestation: Trees naturally absorb carbon dioxide. Massive felling of trees reduces nature's carbon sink, leaving excess CO2 trapped in the atmosphere.
  • (c) Vulnerability of Bangladesh: As a low-lying delta, a slight rise in sea level could submerge a substantial portion of southern coastal Bangladesh, displacing millions.
  • (d) Immediate steps needed: Transitioning to clean renewable energy (solar, wind) and initiating large-scale nationwide tree plantation.

Answer to Question No. 3 (Gap Filling):

(a) industrialization | (b) generating / producing | (c) emission / release | (d) dependence / reliance | (e) forests / trees

Answer to Question No. 4 (Stories):

  • (a) News of Mr. Mallard's death: Richards, Mr. Mallard's close friend, brought the tragic news to Mrs. Mallard after confirming the telegram.
  • (c) Rosamond & The Purple Jar: Rosamond was a young girl who chose a decorative purple jar instead of a sturdy pair of shoes, learning a hard life lesson about superficial vanity.

Answer to Question No. 5 (Poetry):

  • (a) Theme of 'Time, You Old Gipsy Man': The poem highlights the irreversible, fleeting nature of Time and man's futile longing to halt its march.
  • (c) Mary in 'The Sands of Dee': Mary was a poor peasant girl who went to fetch cattle across the river Dee and tragically drowned in an unexpected roaring storm.
  • (d) "Miles to go before I sleep": It symbolizes the numerous moral obligations and promises the poet must fulfill before the final sleep of death.

৬. এসএসসি পরীক্ষায় ইংরেজিতে A+ পাওয়ার বিশেষ কৌশল ও সময় বণ্টন

ইংরেজি ১ম পত্রে ৯০+ নম্বর অর্জন করে নিশ্চিত A+ নিশ্চিত করতে নিচের সময় বণ্টন ও পরীক্ষা হলের গাইডলাইনগুলো মেনে চলা উচিত:

১. রিডিং টেস্টের সময় ব্যবস্থাপনা (১ ঘণ্টা ৪০ মিনিট): প্যাসেজ খুব মনোযোগ দিয়ে রিডিং পড়ার জন্য প্রথম ১০ মিনিট ব্যয় করুন। MCQ ও শর্ট কোয়েশ্চেন লেখার সময় হুবহু প্যাসেজ কপি না করে নিজের ভাষায় ব্যাকরণগতভাবে সঠিক বাক্য গঠন করুন।

২. সামারি লেখার বৈজ্ঞানিক নিয়ম (২০ মিনিট): সামারি মূল প্যাসেজের ৩ ভাগের ১ ভাগ (১/৩) হবে। কোনো উদাহরণ, কোটেশন বা অতিরিক্ত বিবরণ দেওয়া যাবে না।

৩. রাইটিং পার্টের নিখুঁত ড্রাফটিং (১ ঘণ্টা): স্টোরি রাইটিংয়ে আকর্ষণীয় টাইটেল এবং শেষে ১ লাইনের নীতিকথা (Moral) দেওয়া বাধ্যতামূলক। বানান ও বিরামচিহ্ন (Punctuation) সতর্কভাবে পরীক্ষা করুন।

৪. রিভিশন (১০ মিনিট): কোনো উত্তরের ক্রমিক নম্বর ভুল হয়েছে কি না তা নিশ্চিত করতে শেষ ১০ মিনিট খাতা রিভিশন দিন।

৭. সচরাচর জিজ্ঞাসিত প্রশ্নমালা (FAQ)

প্রশ্ন ১: এসএসসি ইংরেজি ১ম পত্রে পাস নম্বর কত?
উত্তর: ইংরেজি ১ম পত্রে ১০০ নম্বরের মধ্যে পাস নম্বর হলো ৩৩। তবে ১ম ও ২য় পত্র মিলিয়ে মোট ২০০ নম্বরের মধ্যে জিপিএ ৫ পেতে হলে মোট ১৬০+ নম্বর পেতে হবে।
প্রশ্ন ২: স্টোরি রাইটিংয়ে টাইটেল না দিলে কি নম্বর কাটা যায়?
উত্তর: হ্যাঁ, কমপ্লিটিং স্টোরিতে একটি উপযুক্ত টাইটেল (Title) এবং শেষে স্পষ্ট নীতিকথা (Moral) না লিখলে ২ থেকে ৩ নম্বর পর্যন্ত কাটা যেতে পারে।
প্রশ্ন ৩: ইংরেজি ১ম পত্রের সিন প্যাসেজ কমন পেতে কী করা উচিত?
উত্তর: এনসিটিবি বোর্ডের মূল পাঠ্যবই (English for Today)-এর গুরুত্বপূর্ণ ইউনিটগুলো বারবার পড়া এবং বিগত ৪-৫ বছরের বোর্ড প্রশ্ন ও টপ স্কুলের মডেল টেস্টগুলো অনুশীলন করা সবচেয়ে কার্যকরী।
